suggestions.rationale: Femoroacetabular impingement, particularly cam-type morphology with an elevated alpha angle, is associated with development and radiographic progression of hip osteoarthritis in systematic-review evidence. The evidence for pincer-type morphology is less consistent. This supports a hip-specific biomechanical/disease-progression research pathway when the individual's documented FAI morphology, symptoms, and osteoarthritis involve the same hip; it does not establish that every person with FAI develops osteoarthritis or that FAI caused an individual case without chronology and competing-risk review.

pathwayIntelligence.causalChain: Documented femoroacetabular impingement morphology, especially cam-type morphology, may produce repetitive abnormal femoroacetabular contact and cartilage/labral damage that contributes to hip osteoarthritis progression in susceptible patients.
developmentQuestions: Is femoroacetabular impingement documented in the same hip as the claimed osteoarthritis, and is the morphology characterized as cam, pincer, or mixed?
Do imaging records document alpha angle, cartilage or labral injury, and subsequent radiographic osteoarthritis progression over time?
Did hip osteoarthritis develop or materially progress after the FAI morphology and symptoms were established?

Which alternative hip-OA contributors such as dysplasia, prior fracture or dislocation, inflammatory arthritis, avascular necrosis, age, weight, and occupational or athletic loading should be addressed?
issuesToResolve: Cam-type evidence is stronger than pincer-type evidence and should not be generalized across all FAI morphologies.
FAI morphology is not sufficient by itself to establish individual causation; same-hip imaging, chronology, and alternative osteoarthritis causes require case-specific review.

evidenceGaps: Hip imaging documenting the FAI morphology and side, including cam/pincer/mixed characterization where available
Longitudinal imaging documenting osteoarthritis onset or progression in the same hip
Clinical chronology of hip symptoms, FAI diagnosis, treatment, and osteoarthritis progression
Assessment of hip dysplasia, trauma, inflammatory disease, avascular necrosis, age, weight, occupational/athletic loading, and other osteoarthritis contributors
Qualified orthopedic opinion addressing the individual biomechanical and chronological relationship

sourceReferences.citation: Kowalczuk M, Yeung M, Simunovic N, Ayeni OR. Does Femoroacetabular Impingement Contribute to the Development of Hip Osteoarthritis? A Systematic Review. Sports Med Arthrosc Rev. 2015;23(4):174-179. PMID 26524551
sourceReferences.note: Systematic review of 35 studies found certain cam-type FAI morphologic features, particularly elevated alpha angle, predispose selected patients to radiographic hip-OA progression; the pincer-type association was less well established. Supports a morphology-specific hip-OA pathway, not automatic individual causation.

nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation under 38 CFR § 3.310 is established by the current evidence; the guard explicitly limits the claim to association.
